issue.title: Filter the device list by site and role
issue.body: The NOC dashboard lists thousands of devices. GET /devices should accept optional query parameters site and role (for example ?site=sjc&role=router) and return only matching devices, still sorted by ID. With no parameters it behaves as today.

requirements.summary: Add optional exact-match 'site' and 'role' query parameters to GET /devices that filter the returned devices (AND semantics when both given), keeping results sorted by ID and preserving current behavior when no parameters are supplied. No matches yields 200 with an empty array.
requirements: GET /devices accepts an optional query parameter 'site' and, when non-empty, returns only devices whose site equals that value.
GET /devices accepts an optional query parameter 'role' and, when non-empty, returns only devices whose role equals that value.
When both 'site' and 'role' are provided, only devices matching both are returned.
Results are always sorted by device ID ascending, whether or not filters are applied.
When no filter parameters are supplied, GET /devices returns all devices exactly as it does today.
When no devices match, the endpoint returns 200 with an empty JSON array.
acceptance_criteria: Given devices in sites sjc and nyc, GET /devices?site=sjc returns status 200 and only devices whose site is sjc, sorted by ID ascending.
Given devices with roles router and switch, GET /devices?role=router returns status 200 and only devices whose role is router, sorted by ID ascending.
Given a mix of devices, GET /devices?site=sjc&role=router returns status 200 and only devices matching both site sjc and role router, sorted by ID ascending.
GET /devices with no query parameters returns status 200 and all devices sorted by ID ascending, identical to the current behavior.
GET /devices?site=unknown where no device has that site returns status 200 and an empty JSON array ([]), not null and not an error.
GET /devices?site=sjc&role=nonexistent where no device matches both returns status 200 and an empty JSON array.
Given devices with IDs inserted out of order, filtered results are still ordered by ID ascending.
GET /devices?site= (empty value) returns status 200 and all devices, treating the empty parameter as not provided.
Matching is exact and case-sensitive: with a device in site sjc, GET /devices?site=SJC returns status 200 and an empty array.
Unrelated query parameters (e.g. ?foo=bar) are ignored and the full list is returned with status 200.
Existing tests for GET /devices without parameters continue to pass unchanged.
assumptions: Site and role are existing string fields on the device model and are populated on stored devices.
Filtering uses exact, case-sensitive string equality; no partial, wildcard, or case-insensitive matching.
When both parameters are given they are combined with AND.
An empty parameter value (?site=) is treated the same as the parameter being absent.
Only a single value per parameter is supported; if a parameter is repeated, the first value is used.
An unknown site or role is not an error; it yields an empty result with status 200 and no validation against a known list of sites or roles.
The response format (JSON array of device objects) and the sort by ID are unchanged from current behavior.
Unknown query parameters are ignored rather than rejected.
Filtering may be done in memory or in the store; the issue does not specify which.
out_of_scope: Pagination, limit, or offset for the device list.
Filtering by any field other than site and role.
Multiple values per parameter (e.g. site=sjc,nyc) or OR semantics.
Case-insensitive, partial, prefix, or wildcard matching.
Changing the sort order or adding sort parameters.
Validation of site or role values against a known list, or 400 responses for bad values.
Performance optimization, indexing, or caching for large device sets.
Changes to other endpoints or to the dashboard UI.

plan.reason: Small, self-contained read-only filter on an existing endpoint. Standard library only. No auth, CI or dependency changes. Requirements are consistent.
steps: In store.go, add func (s *Store) ListFiltered(site, role string) []Device. Take the read lock, keep devices where each non-empty filter equals the field exactly, then sort by ID.
Make ListFiltered start from make([]Device, 0) so no matches encode as [] and never null.
Have List() delegate to ListFiltered("", "") so existing behaviour and sorting stay identical.
In http.go GET /devices, read q := r.URL.Query() and pass q.Get("site") and q.Get("role") to ListFiltered. Get returns the first value and treats empty as absent. Ignore other params.
Add no validation and no new error paths. Response shape stays unchanged.
Run gofmt, go vet and go test.
test_plan: Add table-driven TestStoreListFiltered. Insert devices out of ID order across sites sjc/nyc and roles router/switch.

Store cases: site only, role only, site+role, both empty returns all, unknown site, sjc+nonexistent role, case-sensitive SJC. Each case asserts the exact IDs in ascending order and a non-nil empty slice when nothing matches.
Add table-driven TestHTTPListFilter using httptest. Cases: ?site=sjc, ?role=router, ?site=sjc&role=router, no params, ?site=unknown, ?site=sjc&role=nonexistent, ?site=, ?site=SJC, ?foo=bar.
For each HTTP case, assert status 200, the exact IDs in order, and a body of [] when empty.
Confirm the existing TestHTTPFlow and TestStoreListDelete pass unchanged.

findings.issue: Response bodies in TestHTTPListFilter are never closed, which leaks connections across subtests.
findings.fix: Add defer res.Body.Close() after the error check in TestHTTPListFilter.

findings.issue: On a non-200 status the failure message prints err, which is nil, so it hides the actual status code.
findings.fix: Report the status separately, e.g. t.Fatalf("status %d err %v", res.StatusCode, err), and guard the nil res case.

findings.issue: The error returned by buf.ReadFrom is ignored.
findings.fix: Check the error from buf.ReadFrom and fail the test if it is non-nil.

docs.pr_title: feat(inventory): filter GET /devices by site and role
docs.pr_body:
Closes #2

## What changed
GET /devices now accepts optional `site` and `role` query parameters. When supplied (non-empty), results are limited to devices whose site and/or role exactly match the value; both together combine with AND. Results remain sorted by device ID ascending in all cases.

## Why
The NOC dashboard lists thousands of devices, and operators need to narrow the list by site and role without fetching everything client-side.

## Behavior
- No parameters: unchanged behavior, all devices sorted by ID.
- Empty values (`?site=`) are treated as absent.
- Matching is exact and case-sensitive; `?site=SJC` does not match site `sjc`.
- Unknown site/role yields 200 with `[]`, not an error.
- Unrelated query parameters are ignored.
- Repeated parameters use the first value.

## Files
- `internal/inventory/http.go`: parse `site` and `role` query params and pass them to the store.
- `internal/inventory/store.go`: apply exact-match filtering while preserving ID ordering.
- `internal/inventory/inventory_test.go`: new tests covering single and combined filters, empty and unknown values, case sensitivity, unrelated params, and out-of-order IDs. Existing no-parameter tests are unchanged.

## Testing
Unit tests added in `inventory_test.go` for each acceptance criterion. Existing GET /devices tests pass without modification.

## Out of scope
Pagination, other filter fields, multi-value or OR filters, partial/case-insensitive matching, and validation against known sites or roles.
docs.changelog_entry: Add optional site and role query filters to GET /devices (#2).
api_docs: GET /devices — Optional query parameters: site (exact, case-sensitive match on device site) and role (exact, case-sensitive match on device role). When both are supplied, results must match both (AND). Empty values are treated as absent; repeated parameters use the first value; unknown parameters are ignored. Results are always sorted by device ID ascending. Returns 200 with a JSON array of matching devices, or an empty array [] when none match. Example: GET /devices?site=sjc&role=router
